newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Light grades firm on tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Light grades firm on tight supplies.

text.p: Asian light crudes were steady on Tuesday, with the bulk of trading for September Australian cargoes already completed, traders said.
Most of the September Australian crudes had been committed into the sellers' own systems much earlier, leaving limited supplies on the spot market, they said.
Demand from China and South Korea have absorbed the remaining spot barrels.
Traders said some sellers might decide to sell Kutubu cargoes to take advantage of the firmer prices, but were likely to sell at around Tapis APPI -40/45 cents per barrel.
A western trader was holding a September Tapis cargo, and looking at a premium to Tapis APPI.
Malaysia announced its July crude OSP, reducing the price of Tapis and the other grades by 95 cents per barrel from June.
July Tapis was set at $19.16, compared to $20.11 in June.
Heavy crudes remained quiet.
August barrels of heavy sweet Minas, Widuri and Cinta are still available, but buying interest from Japan was lacklustre, traders said.
In the Middle East crude market, a European major was heard to have bought Oman from a western trader in exchange for Masila.
The European trader was heard to have resold the Oman to a US major at MPM minus one cent per barrel, traders said.
But some traders were uncertain about the deal, as the buyer was heard bidding only at MPM minus five cents per barrel, and was not in a hurry to buy.
But other traders said that this could be the last Oman cargo left for September, which explained the higher level.
Recent Oman trades for September were done around MPM minus three to four cents per barrel.
September Masila was also heard to have been sold by a western trader to another US major at Dubai +30 cents per barrel.
Traders said this equalled to a discount of around 30 cents to the Masila OSP, which was considered a weak level.
But five to ten cargoes of Masila were said to remain available for September, and traders expected prices to fall further.
Qatar released its July official prices, raising the formula of both Qatar Land and Qatar Marine by four cents per barrel to Oman MPM +34, and Oman MPM +1 respectively.
But with the July Oman MPM lowered to $17.46 from $17.75 in June, this would equate to lower outright levels for the Qatar grades.
-- Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3082)
